rationale: Frozen objective is minimizing peak_allocated_bytes for one batch-32 FP32 ResNet-18 inference forward on a single leased CUDA device, subject to images_per_second >= 0.95 of baseline. The torch collector already ran and its evidence (coverage.json: 88/88 CUDA kernels associated, 0 unassociated, 0 root-only, 0 autograd ranges, 0 ambiguous forward sequences) resolves operator-to-kernel attribution completely, so torch is not re-selected and nsys is not selected despite being available: there is no overlap, CUDA-graph-tracing, or attribution question left for it to answer. Selected execution_timeline because the throughput-floor trade-off of any memory-reduction candidate depends on the submit/launch/synchronization structure of the eager forward: its separate plain Torch trace with CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, synchronization events, and per-device intervals shows whether the GPU is submission-bound or compute-bound, while the harness itself already supplies clean per-invocation latency_ms, images_per_second, and peak_allocated_bytes samples; it is used only as structural evidence, never as a communication hook or to determine subsequent search actions, and its clock alignment bounds cover CPU submissions only. Selected python_runtime as a secondary, explicitly perturbing probe of host dispatch and binding costs (warmed cProfile inclusive/self times) to estimate host-side slack available to memory-reduction candidates that alter eager per-layer work; its times are not treated as clean performance scores or GPU compute durations. Excluded nccl_tuning, collective_calibration, and device_telemetry as communication- or device-wide instruments with no question to answer in this single-device, no-backend workload, per the guidance against requesting counters indiscriminately. Excluded candidate_diagnostics and binding_cost because no candidate exists yet this round. Unavailable dimensions are listed with observed reasons rather than estimated or invented.
